title: Fundraising & Field Trips
subtitle: How to submit a fundraiser or a field trip, get approved, and end up on the master calendar.

slides.title: One form. Clear checklist. Official approval.
slides.lede: This replaces paper and email-only requests. The same form covers fundraising (including use of space) and field trips.

cards.b: At least 30 days ahead for a fundraiser or local trip — 60 days for an overnight trip.
Your answers and every file you attach are saved together, so nothing gets lost in an inbox.
Approval alone is not the finish line. If no calendar invite arrives, you are not on the master calendar yet.
The checklist and the forms you need are emailed to you automatically — you do not have to hunt for them.
Fill out the form, attach the required files, then watch your email for the decision.
Get notified the moment you submit, open the review link, and approve or deny with a note.
Files everything, emails the reviewers, emails you the decision, and prepares the calendar entry and field trip forms.

slides.title: Five steps, start to finish
slides.lede: Every request — fundraiser or field trip — follows the same path.

steps.b: Everything is saved and your files are filed together in one place.
With your full summary and a button that opens the review page.
Approve or deny, with an optional note back to you.

steps.h: You get the decision by email
steps.b: Approved or denied. Field trip approvals arrive with your forms attached.
Once the admin adds it to the calendar, you get an invite. That is when it is official.

slides.title: Filling out the form
slides.lede: A step-by-step wizard that only asks what applies to your request.

slides.title: Getting started
slides.lede: Your name, your school email, your grade or group — then pick which kind of request this is.

steps.b: This one choice decides everything you are asked from here on. The form skips anything that does not apply.
It shows Step X of Y and updates as your answers change the path.
Running two separate events? Submit the form twice.

slides.title: Pick Field Trip and it warns you early
slides.lede: Choosing Field Trip pops a banner right away so the paperwork is never a surprise at the end.

steps.b: The full approval checklist is coming on the next steps, along with what you need to attach.
Picking Fundraising skips the trip steps entirely — usually four or five screens.

slides.title: Fundraising details
slides.lede: Covers fundraisers and use of space. Tell it what you are running, when, and where.

steps.b: Chocolates, concessions, ticket sales, fireworks booth, or something else.
Selling for a week? Add a date and time row for each day on the one request.
MPR, CAFE, Turf, Grass, Lobby or Online.
The Main Gym is not on this list — request it from Mike.Cofer@slamnv.org.

slides.note: Main Gym does not go through this form. Email Mike Cofer directly.

slides.title: Money and vendors
slides.lede: What you are charging, what the activity involves, and whether anyone from outside is running it.

steps.b: What families will actually pay.
Answer yes and one more step appears asking you to upload their insurance. Answer no and you skip straight to the agreement.

slides.title: Local or overnight
slides.lede: The single most important answer on a field trip — it changes your deadline and how much paperwork you owe.

steps.b: Minimum 30 days ahead.
Minimum 60 days ahead, and a hotel and rooming step gets added later on.
Pick overnight and the checklist heading, the deadline and the extra hotel section all update on the spot.

slides.title: The pre-approval checklist
slides.lede: Shown in full, in the form, before you are asked for anything — and emailed to you the moment you submit.

steps.b: Charter bus through a local company, admin approval, costs included, quote attached.
Times, activities, cost, lunch plan and what to bring — stapled to the Permission Form and Parent Protocol.
Fingerprinted through Victoria or Maria, listed for approval, waivers to Karla or Cynthia.
Kitchen needs two weeks’ notice through Odalys. Tell the front office the amount, your name and the trip name.

slides.note: The checklist also lists what happens after approval — student spreadsheet, forms to Cynthia or Karla, and picking up the binder on trip day.

slides.title: How you are getting there
slides.lede: Pick the method and the form asks only for that method’s paperwork.

steps.b: Driver and vehicle documentation.
Attach the quote.
Flight options and details.

slides.title: Hotel and rooming
slides.lede: This step only exists if you said overnight.

steps.b: Name, address, contact and phone number.
Check-in and check-out, number of rooms, and how students are assigned.
Confirm the facility meets student safety and supervision requirements.

slides.title: The agreement
slides.lede: One acknowledgement before you submit, on every request type.

steps.b: Communicating details to the front office, getting Cynthia Garcia what she needs on money, supervisor approval for banking and chaperoning, and arranging sub coverage.

slides.title: What happens the second you submit
slides.lede: All of this is automatic. You do not have to email anybody to tell them it is there.

steps.b: Saved with a status of Pending, and your uploads are filed together with a summary.
One email with your full summary and a green Review this request button.

steps.h: Field trips: you get the checklist
steps.b: A pre-approval checklist email lands in your inbox straight away.
There is no decision email yet. That comes after an admin reviews it.

slides.note: Submitting ≠ approved. Approval comes later, by email, then by calendar invite.

slides.title: How it gets approved
slides.lede: What happens on the other side once your request lands.

slides.title: Reviewers get notified
slides.lede: Nobody has to go looking for new requests — the email arrives as soon as you hit submit.

steps.b: Kenny, plus everyone on the Notify List. Add or remove reviewers there without touching the form.
Who submitted, the request type, your full set of answers, and a link to your attached files.
Review this request opens the decision page directly.
If two reviewers open it at once, only the first decision counts — you will never get two conflicting emails.

slides.title: Approve or deny
slides.lede: The review page shows the whole request on one screen, with the files one click away.

steps.b: A pill saying Fundraising or Field Trip, your name and group, every answer you gave, and a link to open your attachments.
Optional on approve, strongly encouraged on deny — it goes to you word for word.
There is a confirmation step, so a stray click cannot email you by accident.
If someone else got there first, the page just shows who decided and when.

slides.title: What you get after a decision
slides.lede: Either way you hear back by email, and you are told what to do next.

cards.b: “Good news — approved”, any note from the reviewer, and a reminder that the calendar invite is the official confirmation.
Permission Form, Parent Field Trip Protocol, Chaperone Waiver and the Student Eligibility Spreadsheet — attached to the approval email.
Fill in the eligibility spreadsheet, and turn the completed forms in to Cynthia or Karla.
You get the reason, and an invitation to revise and resubmit. Nothing is deleted — just fix it and send it again.

slides.title: Approved is not the same as on the calendar
slides.lede: This is the step people miss. Read this one out loud in the meeting.

steps.b: Immediately on approval.

steps.h: The approver gets a second email
steps.b: With an Add to Calendar button, already filled in.

steps.h: They review it and press Save
steps.b: The event goes on the master calendar with you listed as a guest.
A fundraiser gets one entry per date and time row. A field trip gets one all-day event covering the travel dates.

slides.note: No calendar invite means you are not on the master calendar yet. Follow up with the front office.

items: Do I get an email right away? Field trips do — the checklist. The decision email comes later.
Can I edit after submitting? No. Ask to be denied and resubmit, or send a fresh one.
Multiple dates? One form per event, but a fundraiser can carry several date and time rows.
Main Gym? Not through this form — email Mike.Cofer@slamnv.org.
Overnight vs local? Overnight adds the hotel step, a 60-day window and extra checklist items.
Where do my files go? Filed with your request, linked from the reviewer email.

slides.title: Ready when you are
slides.lede: Use the form for every fundraiser and every field trip — it is the only way to get on the master calendar.

steps.b: 30 days for a fundraiser or local trip, 60 for an overnight.

steps.h: Attach the paperwork before you submit
steps.b: A request missing its quote, letter or list will come back to you.
The decision comes there — and for field trips, so do your forms.

steps.h: Check you got the calendar invite
steps.b: That is the confirmation that it is actually booked.
